Short Summary

Natalie presents with confidence, strong relationship-building skills, and potential for outreach. The next interview should validate the depth of her business development experience, the strength of her South Florida network, her SUD expertise, and whether she can independently drive measurable growth.

High-Level Interview Questions

Walk me through the business development strategy you currently own. What market were you responsible for, what goals were established, and what measurable results did you personally produce?

Tell me about your current book of business in detail. Which relationships did you personally develop, how active are they, and what referral volume or revenue have they generated?

If you inherited PRC’s established house accounts, how would you evaluate their health, identify missed opportunities, and create an account-growth strategy without disrupting trusted relationships.

Describe a time you entered a market where you had limited relationships. How did you identify high-value referral sources, earn credibility, and convert outreach activity into admissions?

Based on your substance-use treatment experience, how do you determine whether a referral is clinically appropriate—and how would you position PRC’s PHP, IOP, and dual-diagnosis services to different referral partners?

Just as more context of why she left her last role:
 Her main frustration was micromanagement:
routine work had to go through extra approval channels,
she felt she had to send emails for review before sending them,
she described this as a lack of trust in her judgment and experience.
She also said it was hard to read expectations because the message felt inconsistent:
if she took initiative, the response was “why didn’t you go through me first?”
if she checked first, the response was “why are you asking me?”
On work-life balance, she said there was more travel to the downtown UM location than she expected. She had understood her office would be school-based, so the repeated downtown commute felt misaligned with what she signed up for.
She connected that commute issue to prior experience at Jackson, where traffic/parking stress had also been a reason for leaving.

Rubi's notes: My sister worked in UM and she had the same experience as this candidate. They don't have the best culture.
